analysis.title: October CPI Recap: A jumbo hike is now a live possibility
key_insights: October core CPI printed 0.296% m/m and headline CPI 0.350% m/m, both slightly above expectations. Core rounded to 0.3% for the third month in a row.
Core goods, housing, and core services excluding housing were all lower than in the prior month. The 6m annualized core rate improved to 2.7% from 2.9%, and the 3m annualized rate is 3.75%.
Natixis calls a 0.3% core reading still unacceptably high for the Fed. It says the print adds to the argument that the Fed risks falling behind the curve by not acting decisively.
Fed Governor Waller floated a 50bp hike this morning. Together with sticky inflation, Natixis calls a 50bp December hike a live possibility.

Natixis says the Fed likely would have hiked in October without the market turmoil before that meeting. It describes that volatility as removing another dose of accommodation in the intermeeting period.

Financial conditions are the wildcard. If asset markets avoid more wobbles (especially tech) and growth data stay strong into the Dec 9 meeting, Natixis says it will be hard to argue against a make-up hike for the October pause.
Natixis' base case is still a 25bp hike in December, because this FOMC has signaled gradual, deliberate, and cautious policy.
There is no y/y CPI print this month because of last year's government shutdown.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly above expectations and rounds to 0.3% for the third straight month. Natixis calls this too high for the Fed even though components improved.
Inflation is improving on a 6m basis and is not reaccelerating.
The 3m pace is well above the 6m pace, which supports the Fed-behind-the-curve argument.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed policy rate change, December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Natixis leans toward a gradual 25bp hike, with 50bp a live possibility.

risk_factors: More asset market volatility, especially in tech names, would reduce the case for a December make-up hike.
Strong growth data until the Dec 9 meeting would strengthen the case for a make-up hike.
Further above-consensus inflation prints would increase the odds of a 50bp hike.

tension_points.bull_case: A 50bp hike is a live possibility. Core CPI is still too high, Waller floated the idea, and the Fed risks falling behind the curve. A make-up hike for the October pause would be hard to argue against if markets stay calm and growth stays strong.
tension_points.bear_case: The FOMC has signaled that its preferred policy is gradual, deliberate, and cautious, and inflation is not reaccelerating. Components improved and the 6m annualized rate fell to 2.7%. Natixis therefore leans toward 25bp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Asset markets avoiding more wobbles (especially in tech names) and growth data continuing to show strength until the Dec 9 meeting would make the make-up hike hard to argue against.

theme_stances.key_argument: Sticky core inflation and a make-up for the October pause make a hike likely in December, with 25bp the base case and 50bp possible.
